items.text: All round 2 decisions have been incorporated into plan.md: (1) 700-line mandatory splitting threshold with 500-700 as opportunistic — reflected in Phase 2 strategy and rollout checklist; (2) React decomposition uses sub-components AND custom hooks — GeneratorForm gets section components, pipelineStore gets extracted utility hooks; (3) Early returns + guard clauses are now the explicit primary complexity reduction technique in Phase 3, with helper extraction as secondary; (4) cli/pipeline/commands.go split by command group (commands_run.go, commands_status.go, etc.) is now concrete in the Phase 2 Go files list.

All 8 workshop decisions across rounds 1 and 2 are now reflected in the plan. No open questions or pending decisions remain. The plan covers all four phases (lint setup, file splitting, complexity reduction, validation) with concrete file targets, thresholds, techniques, and validation gates at each step.

Readiness scores are all 3/3. Problem clarity was already strong from GCT evidence. Scope is fully defined with the 700-line threshold and explicit file lists. Approach is solid with ordered phases, concrete techniques (early returns first, then helpers), and per-phase validation. Testability is covered by existing 11-test suite plus golangci-lint and GCT re-review. Risk awareness includes mitigations for import breakage, test flakiness, React prop drilling, and CLI registration.

plan_updates: Incorporated round 2 decisions: 700-line splitting threshold (d1), React sub-component + hook extraction (d2), early returns as primary complexity technique (d3), CLI commands.go split by command group (d4). Tightened Phase 2 and Phase 3 language. Updated rollout checklist to reflect two-tier threshold. Added React prop drilling risk. Plan is now fully decisioned with no open questions.
